I am in Mtwara and my main crop on this small plot is cashew — the nuts grow on trees I have had for many years now. For cashew here, we do not put urea or DAP on the trees; I have never seen my neighbors buy fertilizer for cashew, the money goes to sulphur dust for the flowering time because powdery mildew will spoil the nuts if I do nothing. I will slash the weeds under the trees myself with my panga, and when my son is home from school he helps me collect the nuts. Since my trees are already planted and producing, there is no new seed to buy this season, and cashew here lives on the rains — no one irrigates cashew in my village.
